t: Listen to a talk in a biology class.
Camouflage isn't only about matching the background.
One important type is called disruptive coloration.
Bold stripes or patches break up the outline of an animal's body, so a predator can't easily tell where the animal begins and ends.
Think about a zebra in a moving herd.
The stripes of many animals blend together, and a lion has trouble picking out a single target.
Many fish are dark on top and pale underneath.
Seen from above, the dark back matches the deep water; seen from below, the pale belly matches the bright surface.
It's a bit like a stage designer who lights a set so that the edges of objects disappear.
Some animals, like the cuttlefish, can even change their patterns within seconds.
